column2: Access to the site, storage of materials
The groundwater belongs to the “ground and groundwater conditions” group.
Quiz – setting the foundation level
In Hungarian practice, which factor sets a lower limit on the depth of the foundation level that applies to every site?
The bottom of the topsoil layer
The groundwater level
A uniform 1.0 m

The frost depth is always a lower limit. The groundwater level is rather an upper limit (we found above it if possible), and the bottom of the topsoil varies from site to site and is usually shallower.
What is the frost depth in cohesive soil at 300 m above sea level?
In cohesive soil it is 0.8 m below 500 m above sea level, and 1.0 m above that.
Granular soil, 110 m above sea level, winter groundwater 3 m below the foundation level. What can the frost depth be?
It can be reduced to 0.5 m
0.8 m, it cannot be reduced
Below 500 m above sea level, if the winter groundwater comes no closer than 2.0 m to the foundation level, the frost depth of granular soil can be reduced to 0.5 m.
What soil cover is needed for parts of a building not exposed to frost (e.g. in a basement)?
At least 0.4 m – this is met anyway because of the 50 cm footing depth
At least 0.8 m
No cover is needed
At least 1.5 m
There is no frost risk in the basement, but a minimum cover is needed here too.
In a building with a partial basement, what is the rule for the footing that stays higher?
The natural slope line drawn from its inner edge must not cut the basement wall above the basement floor level
It must be exactly at the frost depth
Its foundation level must be the same as the basement floor
It must be at least 2 m from the basement wall
Otherwise the load of the shallow footing would act on the basement wall, and during excavation the ground could run out from under it.
In stepped deepening, how steep can the line joining the corners be at most?
Any steepness, if the step is under 50 cm
The line joining the corresponding corners of the footings should not be steeper than 30°.
Because of the deeper floor of the new building, its foundation level goes below the neighbour’s old house. What has to be done?
The old one has to be underpinned with concrete or strengthened with jet grouting
Nothing, because the new footing is deeper
The new footing has to be raised above the old one
The old building has to be demolished
Otherwise the ground could run out from under the old footing when the excavation is dug.
Quiz – limit states and design methods
What does the GEO limit state mean?
Failure or excessive deformation of the ground; the resistance is governed by the strength of the ground
Internal failure of structural elements
A change of position as a rigid body
Loss of equilibrium due to uplift
This is the limit state of bearing failure, punching and squeezing of the ground beneath the foundation.
Which two limit states are checked most often for shallow foundations?
GEO and STR
EQU and UPL
UPL and HYD
Bearing failure of the ground (GEO) and the structural adequacy of the footing (STR).
Which one is a serviceability limit state?
Unacceptable vibration
Bearing failure beneath the foundation
Punching through the footing
Uplift
The SLSs: excessive settlement and differential settlement, unacceptable vibration, excessive heave.
When is there a risk of uplift (UPL)?
For lighter structures reaching well below the groundwater level (pool, underpass, underground car park)
For heavy structures above the groundwater
On sloping ground
For foundations on rock
It is often critical only during construction, when the structure is still light.
When is the prescriptive method typically used?
For foundations on rock, with a presumed bearing resistance
For a tower block on soft clay
Always, if there is no ground investigation
For checking uplift
An allowable contact pressure taken from the type, discontinuities and uniaxial compressive strength of the rock (Annex G).
What replaces the design approaches DA1/DA2/DA3 in the 2nd-generation EC7?
The verification cases (VC1–VC4), with the material factor (MFA) or resistance factor (RFA) approach
A single global factor of safety
The allowable stress method
The types of limit state (GEO, STR, EQU, UPL, HYD) remain; it is the verification procedure that changes.
According to the matrix, which category does a CC3 structure with normal geotechnical complexity (GCC2) fall into?
It cannot be classified
High consequence and normal complexity: GC3. The table is a nationally determined parameter.
Quiz – the mechanism of bearing failure
In which stage is the settlement proportional to the load?
I – elastic range
II – transitional range
III – plastic range
In this stage, under constant load the settlement even stops (ds/dt = 0).
What characterises general shear failure?
A slip surface running out to the surface, heave and a distinct peak on the load–settlement curve
A depression of the ground surface without a slip surface
Only plastic zones under the edges of the footing
Creep at constant rate
This is typical in dense granular soil with a shallow foundation, on one side of the footing.
A shallow strip footing on sand with a density index I<sub>D</sub> = 0.5. Which failure is to be expected?
General shear
Local shear
If 0.35 < I<sub>D</sub> < 0.70, local shear failure is to be expected.
What failure typically develops under large reinforced concrete rafts?
Local shear failure under the edges
Deep general shear failure running out to the surface
Squeezing out in the middle of the raft
A deep slip surface cannot form, because the structure is destroyed first by settlements of decimetres.
What characterises punching shear failure?
At most a depression of the ground surface; there is no slip surface in the usual sense
Strong heave on both sides of the foundation
A sudden peak of the curve at small settlement
Rotation of the foundation
It occurs in loose granular and soft cohesive soils; this is also how piles are pushed into the ground.
In the same sand we place the foundation deeper (D/B* increases). Which way does the behaviour shift?
Towards punching
Towards general shear failure
It does not change
Towards uplift
On Vesić’s chart, a larger relative depth needs ever higher density for general shear failure.
At what relative settlement is the peak in general shear failure?
In local shear failure it is 0.07–0.15B, in punching 0.15–0.20B.
The bearing stratum of a shallow foundation is typically within 1–2 m of the surface.
For a building with a basement, close to the superstructure.
For the bearing resistance of a deepened shallow foundation, the shaft resistance is also taken into account.
We use the assumptions made for shallow foundations, i.e. the shaft resistance is neglected.
A piled raft is a mixed (hybrid) foundation system.
It combines the techniques of shallow and deep foundations.
If the near-surface layer is weak but there is nothing better deeper down either, a raft foundation may also be considered.
The weight of the building has to be spread over a large area.
At bridge piers in a river, the risk of scour argues for a deep foundation.
Water can scour and undermine the ground beneath a shallow foundation.
The steps of a brick strip footing are formed horizontally by whole multiples of the brick length.
By whole multiples of half a brick.
For practical reasons, the width and depth of a strip footing are at least 50 cm.
A rule of thumb, for reasons of construction.
In a rubble-concrete strip footing, the stones are distributed evenly over the full depth of the footing.
The rubble stone can be used in a band of about half the depth of the footing.
Mass-concrete strip footings are typically built with formwork today.
